newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end slightly lower.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended slightly lower Friday, correcting downwards from a two week high seen Thursday.

"But the recovery this week has been too technically perfect to believe the month-long downtrend is over or that there's been a big surge of physical demand," Imperial Bank's California-based chief bullion dealer, Jeff Singer, said.

"The recovery still appears to be mostly fund short covering, with the fall in short term gold lease rates back to around 1.40 percent Friday, from a high of 2.00 percent, just confirming the lack of need for gold."
COMEX December gold ended down $1.10 an ounce at $383.40, after trading in a $384.50-382.80 range.
In New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $381.00/381.50 an ounce, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $380.75, and the New York close Thursday at $382.00/382.50.
COMEX December silver ended down 0.2 cent an ounce at $5.058, after trading in a $5.065-5.005 range.
COMEX silver stocks, excluding Wilmington Trust silver stocks, fell a further 2,774,700 ounces Thursday though to 131,012,304 ounces, a new 10-year low.
"But it should be noted that at least some of this metal may return to COMEX approved bank vaults in the next few weeks or months," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
Silver has made the most significant turnaround of the four metals in the precious metals complex, analysts said.
The popular four, nine and 18 day triple-moving-average trend-following indicator has turned into an uptrend for the first time since late August.

The standard nine day relative strength indicator (RSI) has climbed back above 50 percent, but has not yet reached overbought levels above 80 percent, suggesting the recovery may test resistance for December silver is around $5.100 an ounce next week, analysts said.
NYMEX January platinum ended down $2.10 an ounce at $390.00, while NYMEX December palladium closed down 35 cents at $119.00.
